title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde

author.name: Robert Louis Stevenson
author.occupation: Scottish novelist, essayist and travel writer
author.biography: Stevenson grew up in an Edinburgh family of lighthouse engineers, with expectations he would eventually leave behind for writing. Ill health and travel shaped much of his adult life. He had already explored the double life of the respectable criminal Deacon Brodie before writing Jekyll and Hyde in Bournemouth. He later described a dream that supplied part of its story. The novella gives the division between a public reputation and a hidden life the unsettling closeness of two doors in the same city.

hook.text: Which is the real you: the person you show, or the one you hide?

paragraphs: A respectable doctor has made a disturbing arrangement. If he dies or disappears, a man named Edward Hyde is to receive his property. His lawyer, Utterson, cannot understand why his old friend would give such power to someone who seems to inspire immediate disgust.

Utterson suspects that Jekyll is being threatened. He sets out to protect him, with the caution of a man who values loyalty and knows how easily a reputation can be ruined. It is an excellent way into a story about the things respectable people help one another conceal.

Even if the names in the title seem to tell you everything, pay attention to the way Stevenson withholds knowledge. We follow witnesses, documents and half-understood encounters. The city offers doorways into lives that are almost impossible to see whole.

Underneath that mystery lies an attractive possibility: doing what you want without letting it touch the person everyone thinks you are. Many people live with smaller versions of that division. A private indulgence can be explained away as an exception. Then the exception begins to require arrangements of its own.

The horror gathers in those arrangements, in the effort to protect one account of a life while another grows beyond it. Friendship and discretion can preserve a person, but they can also preserve a dangerous secret.
How much of being good depends on what we choose, and how much on the fear that someone might find out?

orientation.text: Begin with Utterson, the lawyer. The story approaches its mystery through his inquiries before letting other voices speak. Let each document arrive in the order Stevenson gives it.

characters.name: Gabriel John Utterson
characters.body: Reserved, loyal and slow to condemn, Utterson is accustomed to keeping other people's affairs private. A disturbing story about Edward Hyde and an unusual clause in Jekyll's will draw him into an inquiry. His concern for his friend has to contend with his reluctance to intrude.

characters.name: Dr. Henry Jekyll
characters.role: A respected doctor with private concerns
characters.body: Prosperous and well regarded, Jekyll belongs to Utterson's circle of old friends. His connection with Edward Hyde is difficult for them to understand. As questions gather around his affairs, his wish to be left alone makes their attempts to help increasingly uneasy.

characters.name: Edward Hyde
characters.role: The unsettling stranger in Jekyll's affairs
characters.body: A man whose conduct alarms witnesses and whose appearance leaves them struggling to explain their disgust. He has access to Jekyll's property and a place in his will. Utterson wants to discover what gives this stranger such a hold over his friend.

characters.name: Dr. Hastie Lanyon
characters.body: A doctor with firm views about respectable science. A professional disagreement has opened a distance between him and Jekyll.

characters.name: Richard Enfield
characters.body: A relative and man about town whose account of a disturbing encounter begins Utterson's inquiry.

characters.name: Poole
characters.body: A longstanding servant with a close view of the household's daily routines. Changes inside the house make that knowledge important.

characters.name: Sir Danvers Carew
characters.body: An elderly gentleman and client of Utterson. His name enters the investigation as it moves beyond a private concern.
